covers.quote: The Vice-Regal Proclamation 1984 sets out the capitalisation of the National Anthem and ‘Advance Australia Fair’.

examples.note: Uses single quotation marks and title case for Advance Australia Fair.

parts.quote: The crowd stood up to listen to the choir sing ‘Advance Australia Fair’.

rules.quote: Use title case (maximal capitalisation) and quotation marks for Australia’s National Anthem.
rules.violation_condition: Australia's National Anthem ('Advance Australia Fair') written without quotation marks or without title case
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Direct rule on styling the Australian National Anthem.

examples.note: Unnamed composition in roman type without quotation marks.

parts.quote: Telemann’s suite in D major, TWV 55:C6, was the first piece our chamber group performed in public.

rules.quote: For compositions with no given name, use roman type and no quotation marks.
rules.violation_condition: a musical composition with no given name (identified by key, type, or number) formatted in italics or in quotation marks
rules.why: G-4: Body sentence states the formatting rule for unnamed musical compositions.

examples.note: Capital 'D' used for key.

parts.quote: Telemann’s suite in D major, TWV 55:C6, was the first piece our chamber group performed in public.

rules.quote: Always use a capital letter for the key of musical compositions.
rules.violation_condition: the key letter of a musical composition written in lower case
rules.why: Distinct orthographic rule for musical keys.

examples.note: Contraction 'no' without a full stop.

parts.quote: The radio was playing Elena Kats-Chernin’s piano concerto no 3.

rules.quote: For compositions numbered as one of a series, do not use a full stop for the contraction for the word numero (or ‘number’).
rules.violation_condition: 'no.' with a full stop when used for numbered musical compositions
rules.why: Specific rule prohibiting a full stop in 'no' for numbered compositions.

examples.note: Lower case 'concertos'.

parts.quote: Vivaldi composed several concertos for strings; my favourite is Op. 12.

examples.note: Lower case 'string quartets'.

parts.quote: Australian composer Carl Vine composed 6 string quartets between 1979 and 2017.

rules.quote: Don’t capitalise the generic type of composition.
rules.violation_condition: a generic type of composition (such as concerto, symphony, quartet) written with an initial capital letter
when: Foreign terms that are part of the title of the composition may retain title capitalisation.
rules.why: Clear instruction not to capitalise generic musical types.

covers.quote: * Use the foreign terms if they are part of the title of the composition.

rules.quote: Use the English word for most types of compositions (Table 1).
rules.violation_condition: a non-English musical term used instead of its preferred English counterpart when not part of the composition's proper title
when: Use foreign terms if they are part of the title of the composition.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Combines preference for English terms with its specific exception in Table 1 footnote.

covers.quote: Use ‘concertos’, not ‘concerti’. The exception is ‘concerti grossi’,* the name for a particular style of composition.

rules.quote: Use the English plural form for most types of compositions (Table 2).
rules.violation_condition: a foreign plural form (such as concerti) used instead of the English plural (concertos)
when: The exception is 'concerti grossi', the name for a particular style of composition.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Combines pluralisation rule with Table 2 note exception.

examples.note: Op. written with a full stop.

parts.quote: Vivaldi composed several concertos for strings; my favourite is Op. 12.

rules.quote: Always use a full stop with this abbreviation.
rules.violation_condition: the abbreviation 'Op' for opus written without a full stop
rules.why: Specific punctuation rule for 'Op.'.

rules.quote: Never spell out these shortened forms.
rules.violation_condition: spelling out catalogue abbreviations such as 'opus' or 'Bach Werke Verzeichnis' instead of 'Op.' or 'BWV'
rules.why: Direct prohibition against spelling out catalogue designations.

covers.quote: Composition titles can be the name that the composer or producer gave the work or they can be a popular name. The titles of hymns follow the same style.
If a title is in another language, refer to it in the original language unless it has an English title. Apply the capitalisation rules of the original language.

examples.note: Song title in single quotes and sentence case.

parts.quote: The town meeting ended with the school children singing ‘The road to Gundagai’.

examples.note: Song title in single quotes and sentence case.

parts.quote: Justine Clarke became well known among Australian children for her 2005 song ‘I like to sing’.

examples.note: Popular and given names of short pieces/subtitles in single quotes.

parts.quote: Many people know Beethoven’s piano sonata no 14 ‘Quasi una fantasia’ as the ‘Moonlight sonata’.

examples.note: Non-English title using original capitalisation inside single quotes.

parts.quote: Clara Schumann’s ‘Wenn ich ein Vöglein wär’ was arranged as a 3-part canon.

rules.quote: Place the titles of songs or short, discrete pieces in single quotation marks. Use sentence case.
rules.violation_condition: the title of a song, hymn, or short discrete piece written without single quotation marks, or written in title case or italics
when: If a title is in another language, refer to it in the original language unless it has an English title, and apply the capitalisation rules of that language.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Core styling rule for songs and short pieces.

examples.note: Uses 'ft' without a period.

parts.quote: Number 5 on Triple J’s Hottest 100 in 2014 was ‘Take me over’ by Peking Duk ft SAFIA.

rules.quote: Use the abbreviation ‘ft’ for artists named as featuring on song recordings.
rules.violation_condition: using 'feat.', 'featuring', or 'ft.' instead of 'ft' without punctuation for featuring artists
rules.why: Specific abbreviation rule for featuring artists.

covers.quote: Use italics and sentence case for the titles of albums, compilations, playlists and collections. Use the same punctuation as the original title of the album or compilation.
For names of the soundtracks of films and video games, use italics and sentence case. For individual pieces in the soundtrack, use single quotation marks and roman type.

examples.note: Operas in italics and sentence case.

parts.quote: Many people know Australian tenor David Hobson from La bohème and The pirates of Penzance. Fewer people know that he is the composer of the chamber opera Remembering Rosie.

examples.note: Collection title in italics and sentence case.

parts.quote: The Brandenburg concertos are part of Bach’s collection of concertos (BWV 1046–1051).

rules.quote: Use italics and sentence case for the titles of long works.
rules.violation_condition: title of a long musical work (such as an opera, ballet, musical, or album) written without italics or in title case
when: If the title is in a language other than English, refer to it in the original language and apply the capitalisation rules of that language.
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Consolidates italics and sentence case across long works, albums, compilations, and soundtracks.

covers.quote: If you mention the name of the song in the text, place only the author and the year in parentheses. If you mention the author in text, put the date in parentheses straight after the author’s name.
Use single quotation marks and sentence case for the name of the song.

examples.note: Lyric citation with author, song title, and year in parentheses.

parts.quote: Kevin Parker sings, ‘If it calls you, embrace it / If it haunts you, face it’. We can all learn from that (Tame Impala, ‘Lost in yesterday’ 2020).

rules.quote: Write the name of the song, the author and the year of publication in parentheses when you cite lyrics in a text.
rules.violation_condition: citing lyrics in text without author, song title (in single quotes and sentence case), and year in parentheses (adjusting for items named in the running text)
when: If you mention the name of the song in the text, place only the author and the year in parentheses.
If you mention the author in text, put the date in parentheses straight after the author’s name.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Citing lyrics in-text with its placement variants.

examples.note: Author-date reference list entry for a song.

parts.quote: Tones and I (2019) ‘Dance monkey’ [Song], The kids are coming, Sony Music Australia.

rules.quote: Rule: Creator C (Year) ‘Title of song: subtitle of song’ [Medium], Title of compilation or album, Name of Publisher.
rules.violation_condition: a reference list entry for a song that does not follow the format: Creator C (Year) ‘Title of song: subtitle of song’ [Medium], Title of compilation or album, Name of Publisher.
rules.why: Author-date reference list template for songs.

examples.note: Reference entry for an album.

parts.quote: Farnham J (1968) Sadie[Album], EMI/Columbia.

examples.note: Reference entry for a classical compilation album.

parts.quote: Bach JS (2010) The Brandenburg concertos: concertos BWV 1043 & 1060 [Album recorded by Academy of St Martin in the Fields], Decca.

rules.quote: Rule: Creator C (Year) Title of long work or compilation[Medium], Name of Publisher.
rules.violation_condition: a reference list entry for a long musical work or album that does not follow the format: Creator C (Year) Title of long work or compilation[Medium], Name of Publisher.
rules.why: Author-date reference list template for long musical works / compilations.
